# Design System

> **Steering, not spec.** This captures the *durable direction and rules* of matthewfield.ca's
> visual system — principles, semantic roles, usage rules, governance, and non-negotiable gates.
> The *concrete values that churn* (exact palette/token values, the precise type scale,
> per-component and per-surface decisions) live in the design spec / implementation and in the
> token source of truth, not here. This is a **direction-light** system on purpose: the visual
> identity is deliberately left open and resolved in the design spec. Where a value is not yet
> decided, the section says **`Deferred: …`** rather than committing prematurely.

## Purpose

Guarantee that every page and component across the site reads as one coherent, professional,
fast presence — consistent type, color, spacing, surfaces, and interaction — so the design
supports the product's inbound-funnel goal rather than fighting it. This document fixes the
*rules and direction*; the exact look is set in the design spec.

## Scope: What Belongs Here vs. in a Spec

- **Here (steering):** principles, semantic token roles, usage rules, accessibility/performance/theme
  gates, surface and motion language, governance.
- **In a spec / in code:** exact palette and token values, the precise type scale, per-component and
  per-surface decisions, the migration of the eight already-built sections, and the token source of
  truth (`src/styles/tokens.css`).
- **Applies to** the `(site)` route group (landing, profile, projects, contributions, blog,
  resources, slash pages). **Excludes** the `(playground)` route group — it is intentionally
  style-isolated (`all: initial` + `isolation: isolate` + `@layer playground`) and owns its own
  presentation.
- **Don't restate the other steering docs** — cross-reference them: `product.md` for vision/tone and
  the experience principles, `tech.md` for the delivery mechanism (Tailwind v4, shadcn, `next-themes`,
  the build/CSP), `structure.md` for where CSS and components live.

## Design Principles

1. **Wide & spacious.** Generous, rhythmic whitespace; long-form prose held to a ~75-character
   measure. Spaciousness comes from breathing room, not from stretching text to the edge.
2. **Restraint over decoration.** Minimal and precise — the design should signal infra/platform
   craft and feel like a person's home, not a corporate template.
3. **Accessible by default.** Semantic HTML, AA contrast in both themes, visible focus, full
   keyboard support. Accessibility is a gate, not a polish pass.
4. **Both themes are first-class.** Light and dark are designed as a matched pair, never one
   derived from the other.
5. **Fast is a feature.** Every visual choice lives within the performance budget; no unnecessary
   client JS on content pages.
6. **Roles, not one-offs.** Components consume semantic tokens (`bg-primary`, `text-muted-foreground`),
   never literal values.

## Color

[Roles and rules here; concrete values live in the token source of truth.]

- **Semantic roles:** `background`/`foreground`, `card`, `popover`, `primary`, `secondary`, `muted`,
  `accent`, `destructive`, `border`, `input`, `ring`, plus chart and sidebar roles. The role
  *taxonomy* is durable; new roles are added only when an existing one cannot express a genuine need.
- **Usage rules:** every text/UI use of a role must clear its contrast gate in both themes (see
  Gates). Secondary text uses `muted-foreground`; destructive/danger surfaces use `destructive`.
  Some role values are already tuned away from the shadcn defaults specifically to pass contrast.
- **Theming:** light (`:root`) and dark (`.dark`) are a matched pair toggled by `next-themes`
  (class on `<html>`, `@custom-variant dark`); parity is expected and verified.
- **Concrete values:** `Deferred:` — authored in `src/styles/tokens.css` (OKLCH). The palette is
  currently fully neutral (zero-chroma); **whether an accent hue / chroma is introduced is decided in
  the design spec.**

## Typography

- **Type roles:** display/headings (`h1`–`h6`, mapped to semantic HTML in order), body, secondary/meta,
  and code. Emphasis never substitutes for correct heading structure.
- **Font families:** Geist Sans (`--font-sans`, UI/headings/body) and Geist Mono (`--font-mono`, code),
  self-hosted via `next/font` (the content-page CSP forbids external font origins).
- **Usage rules:** components pick a scale step; they do not invent ad-hoc sizes. Prose holds the
  ~75-character measure.
- **Exact scale & voice:** `Deferred:` — the precise scale (ratio/steps/line-heights) and whether the
  voice changes beyond Geist (a display face, weight/letterspacing personality) are decided in the
  design spec.

## Spacing & Layout

- **Spacing approach:** a single consistent spacing scale governs margin/padding/gap; whitespace, not
  one-off values, creates the "wide & spacious" feel.
- **Grid / breakpoints:** responsive with mobile as a first-class target (recruiters on phones);
  nothing is desktop-only. Gallery surfaces (blog, projects, contributions) share the shadcn `Card`
  grid for visual consistency.
- **Density:** comfortable by default. The professional profile is the documented wide-layout
  exception (more viewport width than standard content pages).
- **Motion (optional):** purposeful and restrained — clarifies state/relationship, never decorates.
  *Whether* motion is used and its easing/duration is `Deferred:` to the design spec; reduced-motion
  handling is covered under Accessibility, and any motion must stay within the performance gate.

## Components

[Cross-cutting conventions, not a catalog — per-component specifics belong in specs.]

- **Naming & structure:** shadcn/ui primitives are owned source in `src/components/ui/`; other
  components compose them (composition over forking the primitive). File/exports per `structure.md`.
- **Required states:** every interactive component handles, as applicable, default / hover /
  **visible focus** / active / disabled / loading / error.
- **Variant policy:** introduce variants sparingly via the primitive's API; gallery cards share the
  `Card` container (border/radius/padding/shadow/hover) so only the inner content varies by type.
- **Component library:** shadcn/ui on Radix primitives is the source of truth for behavior and ARIA;
  lucide is the icon set.

## Accessibility & Non-Negotiable Gates

Blocking bars every UI change must clear — gates, not aspirations. A design that fails these is not
"bold," it is incorrect.

- **Accessibility:** WCAG 2.1 AA contrast (≥4.5:1 normal text) in **both** themes, enforced by
  axe-core in the E2E suite (blocking); visible focus on all interactive elements; full keyboard
  support; `prefers-reduced-motion` respected; correct ARIA via Radix primitives; alt text on all
  images.
- **Performance:** static pages hold a 90+ Lighthouse score (blocking) — bounds webfonts, imagery,
  animation, and added client JS. Mirrors `product.md`'s "no unnecessary JavaScript on content pages."
- **Theme parity:** every surface verified in both themes, no regressions on toggle.
- **Responsive:** every surface verified at mobile, tablet, and desktop widths.
- Gates apply to the `(site)` group; the isolated playground is exempt.

## Design Tokens (source of truth)

- **Source of truth:** `src/styles/tokens.css` — OKLCH values in matched `:root` (light) + `.dark`
  pairs, plus the single `--radius` dial (with `sm/md/lg/xl` derived) that drives all corner rounding.
  Steering points here; it does not duplicate concrete values.
- **Consumption:** the `@theme inline` block in `src/styles/globals.css` maps each token to a Tailwind
  utility (`--color-<role>` → `bg-<role>`/`text-<role>`); components use the utilities, never literals.
- **Naming convention:** semantic role names (`<role>` / `<role>-foreground`) as CSS custom properties
  (`--<role>`); per-section styles live under `src/styles/`.

## Governance & Ownership

**The design system owns the token values; shadcn/ui is a point of departure, not an upstream we
track.** This reverses the prior "regenerate from shadcn / do not hand-edit `tokens.css` / stay
byte-aligned with upstream" rule — the project has already diverged for accessibility, and a
first-class design system needs to author and tune tokens against *this* system. `tokens.css` is the
implementation of this document; when they disagree, this document wins and the file is corrected.
shadcn's neutral/new-york defaults are retained where they serve and overridden where the system
requires. Specs request new roles only when an existing role cannot express a need.

> Follow-on: the old "regenerate from shadcn" notes in `tech.md`/`structure.md` and the header
> comments in `tokens.css`/`globals.css` should be updated to match this ownership model (tracked as
> part of the design-system rollout, not this document).

## Deferred Decisions

The visual identity is intentionally **not** fixed here — it is chosen and adversarially
pressure-tested in the design spec's requirements phase. Open and owned by the spec:

- **Direction:** refine the current neutral/minimal look vs. introduce a distinct brand identity —
  `Deferred: design spec (requirements)`.
- **Palette / chroma:** whether an accent hue is introduced, and exact OKLCH values for every role in
  both themes — `Deferred: design spec; values live in tokens.css`.
- **Typographic voice & scale:** any face/weight personality beyond Geist, and the precise scale —
  `Deferred: design spec`.
- **Motion presence:** whether motion is used and its style, within the performance gate —
  `Deferred: design spec`.
- **Elevation language:** whether a tokenized shadow/elevation set is introduced (the system is
  currently flat/bordered) — `Deferred: design spec`.

## Voice & Tone

Professional but warm — "a person's home on the internet, not a corporate template" (see `product.md`
for the full tone). Interface microcopy stays concise and human; long-form copy gets a plain-English
pass. Detailed content conventions are out of scope for this document.
